title: fix: consent app card layout on narrow screens
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
The app card on the authorize screen put the redirect host on the right with `shrink-0`, so on phones it squeezed the app name and developer link into wrapped fragments ("Pollinations / ↵ Playground", "@pollinations- ↵ ai").

- Stack the card into one full-width line per field: app name, site, developer
- Every line shares the icon column used by the consent rows below; "by" takes that slot on the developer line
- Make the site clickable (opens the origin only, never the redirect URL with its OAuth params; non-http schemes stay plain text)
- Show the developer as a compact profile pill (avatar, handle, external arrow); the whole pill links to their profile
- Add `AccountIdentityLink` to `@pollinations/ui` so other screens can reuse the pill

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| Host top-right, name and handle wrap mid-word | Name / site / `by` pill, one line each, aligned |

Checked on the real `/authorize` page against a local Enter + D1: phone and desktop, dark and light, signed in and signed out, long app/host/handle names.

gist.headline: Room to read the fine print
gist.blurb: The authorize screen’s app card now gives the name, site, and developer their own space on phones. The site opens its origin, not an OAuth redirect full of parameters.
gist.summary: Reworked the /authorize app card into aligned, full-width name, site, and developer rows; the site links only to HTTP(S) origins, and a reusable AccountIdentityLink provides the developer profile pill.
gist.impact: On narrow screens, app names and handles are easier to read, users can inspect the app’s site without opening its redirect URL, and the developer pill links to their profile.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a narrow phone showing a tidy authorization card with three aligned rows: app name, site, and a small developer avatar pill. Polli, wearing tiny reading glasses, checks the site link; a flowering vine beside the phone adds a gentle growth motif.
